A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Hierarchical Speculative Decoding work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite pagination changes and the added implementation appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original decoding-efficiency and task-accuracy experiments, including main Tables 1–4, appendix ablations and repeated-run results, and a runtime breakdown.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in Tables 1–4 and A.1–A.4, including benchmark comparisons, ablations, and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The hierarchical verification procedure, capped ratios, acceptance and resampling equations, and Algorithms 1–3 remain unchanged. Appendix F newly documents an implementation; parallel masking was already described in v1's Appendix G.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate mathematical problem solving on GSM8K, code generation on HumanEval, and summarization on CNN/DailyMail. The single-draft, multi-draft, and EAGLE-3 scenarios are retained without added coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged across the corresponding Tokenwise, Blockwise, recursive rejection sampling, and EAGLE-3 comparisons. Newly cited CoS is not added to the evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The reported model pairs, quantization, hardware, temperature and draft-length settings, 11-candidate multi-draft protocol, and evaluation metrics are retained. The added description of EAGLE-3 drafting supplies context for an existing experiment rather than documenting a revised protocol.

E4.justification: The temperature and draft-length ablations, capping ablation, task-accuracy checks, acceptance analysis, and runtime breakdown are unchanged. The revised EAGLE-3 explanation is not accompanied by a new diagnostic experiment.

E5.justification: Table A.1 reports the same means and standard deviations across five differently seeded runs in both versions, and Table A.3 retains its uncertainty reporting. The new mention of sampling stochasticity introduces no additional uncertainty estimate or statistical test.

E6.justification: The reported results in Tables 1–4 and A.1–A.4 and Figure A.1 are unchanged. For example, Table 4b retains EAGLE-3 versus EAGLE-3H block efficiencies of 3.40 versus 3.55 and decoding speeds of 71.59 versus 80.49. Their causal interpretation changes, rather than their values.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, branch-divergence results, losslessness proofs, and expected-acceptance derivations in the main text and Appendices A–D are retained. Equation spacing and pagination change without substantive mathematical revisions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the lossless HSD claim, average 6.7% decoding-speed improvement, and over-12% EAGLE-3 gain. The new qualification in Section 6.2 does not revise these headline claims.

C2.justification: Section 6.2 substantially reinterprets a headline experiment. Where v1 presents EAGLE-3 integration as evidence of improved verification efficiency, v2 states that its draft-probability setting makes verifiers theoretically equivalent, attributes the block-efficiency difference to stochasticity and floating-point precision, and attributes the speedup to avoiding explicit verification loops.

D1.justification: New Appendix F substantially expands implementation disclosure with Tokenwise and HSD PyTorch listings, tensor shapes, sampling and stopping logic, and Transformers v4.46.3 provenance. v1 supplied pseudocode, implementation discussion, and the same repository link. v2 also newly describes the existing EAGLE-3 drafting setting.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Fan et al. on draft-model training, Fu et al. on CoS, Peng et al. on LMM-R1, Yu et al. on DAPO, and Wolf et al. on Transformers. These are limited contextual and implementation additions; the central positioning against existing verification methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 tightens portions of Section 6, combines the Llama and EAGLE-3 discussion, and inserts the implementation appendix. Former Appendices F and G become G and H. The main narrative and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds two formatted code listings, shortens Table 3's subcaptions, and adjusts equation spacing and page flow. Existing figures and table structures are preserved; relocated material does not constitute new evidence.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves transparency by qualifying the unchanged EAGLE-3 result and exposing implementation details in Appendix F. These gains are limited: the headline claims remain unqualified, and printed Listing 2 uses n_matches before assigning it, obstructing straightforward execution. The revision makes the work easier to interpret and audit, but leaves important reproducibility and claim-alignment issues unresolved.
